To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

inhibition of VEGF in prepubertal rats treated with eCG results in a decrease in the number of perivulatory follicles and an increase in the number and percentage of atretic antral follicle, which is accompanied by a significant increase in apoptosis.
the inhibition of VEGF in the prepubertal rat ovary leads to an imbalance in the BCL2 protein family members, thus increasing apoptosis and decreasing the number of follicles that ovulate.
the local inhibition VEGFA activity increases the number of apoptoses in preovulatory follicles, leading to a decrease in ovulation and a larger number of atretics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible role of VEGFA in follicle survival during the gonadotropins-induced folliculogenesis.
the role of the vascular endothelial growth factors (VEGFA and VEGFB) in the regulation of the folliculogenesis.
the role of VEGFA in the intraovarian regulation of folliculogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

VEGF is a critical intraovian survival factor in gonadotrophin-dependent folliculogenic processes, and that the inhibition of VEGF activity in the ovary leads to a higher rate of follicular atresia, mainly in EAFs and periovulatory follicle stages.
VEGFA is a survival factor for follicular development and that its inhibition causes an increase in follicular apoptosis.
VEGFA plays a critical role in the intraovarian survival of follicles in gonadotro-pin-treated prepubertal rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VEGFA is a survival factor in the gonadotropins-dependent preantral and antral follicle development.
the inhibition of VEGF in the ovary of prepubertal rats causes an imbalance in the expression of the antiapoptotic protein BCL2, leading to a higher rate of follicular atresia.
inhibition of VEGF activity by Trap leads to an increase of BAX/BCL2L1 ratio in antral follicle and consequently, an increase in apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intraovarian VEGF/FLT1 system is critical for follicular survival during folliculogenesis.
VEGFA appears to be a survival factor that is critical in gonadotrophin-dependent folliculogensis in the prepubertal rat.
the inhibition of VEGF in the ovary leads to a higher rate of follicular atresia, which is mediated, at least in part, through a BCL2 family-dependent mechanism.
